# Notebar — Design Spec

- **Date:** 2026-08-29
- **Status:** Draft, pending approval
- **Platform:** macOS 26+ (Apple Silicon), Windows as a later, separate shell

---

## 1. Purpose

Notebar is an always-available scratch surface that lives at the right edge of the
screen. It stays invisible until the cursor reaches the edge, then slides out as a
floating overlay above whatever app is in front — including fullscreen apps. It holds
notes and tasks that can reference each other, so a thought captured while working can
become a tracked task without leaving the current context.

The design goal is **zero-friction capture**. Anything that makes the user think about
Notebar as an application — activating it, finding its window, losing their place — is a
defect.

### Success criteria

1. Cursor to edge → panel fully expanded in under 250 ms.
2. Capturing a note from any app requires no click on any window but Notebar's.
3. The panel never collapses while the user is mid-thought (typing, dragging, menu open).
4. Idle cost is under 1% CPU and under 150 MB RAM.
5. No permission prompt on first launch.

### Non-goals for v1

Cloud sync, multi-device, sharing, collaboration, mobile, plugins, AI features,
calendar integration, and reminders/notifications. The schema is designed not to
preclude sync; nothing is built for it.

---

## 2. Decisions

| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Stack | Native SwiftUI + AppKit, Swift 6.3 | Best possible macOS feel: real `NSPanel` edge docking, native drag-and-drop, lowest idle footprint, best animation quality. |
| Windows strategy | Rewrite the shell later; share the core | All domain logic lives in a pure-Swift package with no Apple-UI imports, so the Windows port rewrites the UI, not the app. |
| Activation | Invisible, cursor-position polling | No visible sliver, no Accessibility permission. |
| Note content | Rich text (WYSIWYG) | Formatting, checkboxes, and inline link chips without markup noise. |
| Storage | Local SQLite only | Relational from day one so links, backlinks, and board ordering are queries, not bookkeeping. |
| Minimum OS | macOS 26.0 | Only SDK installed; unlocks current SwiftUI text and material APIs. |

### Decisions made on the user's behalf

These were not asked about. Each is reversible and flagged for review.

1. **Board columns are data, not an enum.** Seeded with Queue / Working / Done, but
   stored as rows so user-defined statuses in v2 need no migration.
2. **Rich text persists as RTF, not an archived `AttributedString`.** RTF is documented
   and portable; the data survives leaving this app.
3. **Open note tabs persist across restarts.** Matches the Notepad++ mental model the
   user referenced — the session is part of the state.
4. **The Tasks board is responsive to panel width** — stacked status groups when narrow,
   side-by-side kanban when wide. See §6.

---

## 3. Architecture

```
Notebar/
├── Notebar/                        app target · AppKit + SwiftUI · macOS-only
│   ├── App/                        NotebarApp, AppDelegate, MenuBarExtra, LaunchAtLogin
│   ├── Panel/                      EdgePanel, HotEdgeMonitor, PanelStateMachine, PanelAnimator
│   ├── Features/
│   │   ├── Notes/                  NotesTabView, NoteTabStrip, NoteEditor, QuickOpen
│   │   ├── Tasks/                  TasksTabView, BoardView, GroupedListView, TaskCard, DragCoordinator
│   │   └── Settings/               SettingsTabView (shell only in v1)
│   ├── Linking/                    MentionAutocomplete, LinkChipAttachment, BacklinksView
│   └── DesignSystem/               Tokens, Chrome, Buttons, EmptyStates
└── Packages/NotebarKit/            PURE SWIFT · zero AppKit / SwiftUI imports
    ├── Models/                     Note, Task, Board, BoardColumn, Link, Tag, OpenTab
    ├── Store/                      Schema, Migrations, Repository protocols, GRDB impls
    ├── Search/                     SearchIndex (FTS5)
    └── Linking/                    LinkGraph, BacklinkResolver
```

### The NotebarKit rule

`NotebarKit` must never import `AppKit`, `SwiftUI`, or `UIKit`. This is the entire
Windows strategy expressed as one constraint, and it is enforced mechanically:

```bash
! grep -rE '^import (AppKit|SwiftUI|UIKit)' Packages/NotebarKit/Sources/
```

This check runs in CI and as a pre-commit hook. Storage lives behind repository
protocols (`NoteRepository`, `TaskRepository`, `LinkRepository`), with GRDB as the
macOS implementation, so the Windows port swaps the implementation rather than
rewriting call sites.

---

## 4. The panel

### 4.1 Window configuration

An `NSPanel` subclass, not an `NSWindow`:

| Property | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `styleMask` | `[.nonactivatingPanel, .borderless, .fullSizeContentView]` | Accepts keystrokes without activating the app, so typing into the overlay does not disturb the frontmost app's state. |
| `level` | `.floating` | Above normal windows, below system UI. |
| `collectionBehavior` | `[.canJoinAllSpaces, .fullScreenAuxiliary, .stationary]` | Follows the user across Spaces and appears over fullscreen apps. |
| `hidesOnDeactivate` | `false` | Managed by the state machine, not by AppKit. |
| `isFloatingPanel` | `true` | Panel semantics. |
| `isMovable` | `false` | Position is owned by the edge dock. |

The app itself is `LSUIElement` — no Dock icon, no menu bar of its own. A `MenuBarExtra`
provides quit, settings, and a manual toggle.

### 4.2 Hot edge detection

```
CVDisplayLink / Timer
  └── NSEvent.mouseLocation          (static property; no permission, no entitlement)
        ├── idle          10 Hz      cursor far from any edge
        └── near edge     60 Hz      cursor within 80 pt of the active screen's right edge
```

`NSEvent.mouseLocation` requires no Accessibility or Input Monitoring permission,
which is what makes the fully-invisible activation viable without a first-run prompt.

The active screen is the one whose frame contains the cursor, so multi-monitor works by
construction. Only that screen's right edge is a trigger in v1; edge and screen choice
become settings later.

**Known limits.** Polling does not observe the cursor while another app holds an
exclusive cursor grab (some games), and coordinates are unavailable during certain
secure-input contexts. Both degrade to "panel does not open," which is acceptable. The
global hotkey remains available as an escape hatch in all cases.

### 4.3 State machine

```
        ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │                                              │
        ▼                                              │
   ┌─────────┐  edge dwell   ┌───────────┐  anim done  │
   │ hidden  │──────────────▶│ expanding │────────────▶│
   └─────────┘   ≥120 ms     └───────────┘             │
        ▲                                              ▼
        │                                       ┌────────────┐
        │                          pin ────────▶│  expanded  │
        │                                       └────────────┘
        │                                          │      ▲
        │                          exit dwell      │      │ re-entry
        │                          ≥350 ms         ▼      │ cancels
   ┌────────────┐   anim done   ┌────────────┐            │
   │  hidden    │◀──────────────│ collapsing │────────────┘
   └────────────┘               └────────────┘
```

`pinned` is a flag on `expanded`, not a separate state; it suppresses every collapse
trigger except an explicit unpin or `⌘W`.

**Timings** (all user-tunable in Settings later):

| Constant | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `edgeDwell` | 120 ms | Cursor must rest in the trigger zone this long before expanding. Prevents accidental opens when crossing to a scrollbar. |
| `triggerWidth` | 2 pt | Width of the trigger zone at the screen edge. |
| `exitSlop` | 24 pt | Cursor must leave the panel frame by this margin before the exit timer starts. |
| `exitDwell` | 350 ms | Cursor must stay outside for this long before collapsing. |
| `expandDuration` | 180 ms | Spring animation in. |
| `collapseDuration` | 140 ms | Slightly faster out than in — feels responsive rather than sluggish. |

### 4.4 Collapse suppression

This is the difference between a panel that feels alive and one that feels hostile. The
naive implementation collapses on `mouseExited` and is unusable: the panel vanishes when
the user reaches for a menu, drags a card, or glances away mid-sentence.

Collapse is suppressed while **any** of the following hold:

- The panel is pinned.
- A menu, popover, or sheet spawned by the panel is open.
- A drag operation is in flight.
- The panel window is key **and** a text editor has first responder.
- A keystroke was received within the last `typingGrace` interval.

The precise policy is a genuine judgment call and is left for the user to author —
see §9.

---

## 5. Data model

```sql
CREATE TABLE note (
  id           TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  title        TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  body_rtf     BLOB,                    -- NSAttributedString RTF round-trip
  body_plain   TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',-- shadow column, kept in sync on save
  is_pinned    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  sort_order   REAL    NOT NULL,
  created_at   TEXT NOT NULL,
  updated_at   TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE board (
  id           TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  name         TEXT NOT NULL,
  sort_order   REAL NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE board_column (
  id           TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  board_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES board(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  name         TEXT NOT NULL,
  kind         TEXT NOT NULL,           -- backlog | active | done
  sort_order   REAL NOT NULL,
  wip_limit    INTEGER
);

CREATE TABLE task (
  id           TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  title        TEXT NOT NULL,
  detail_rtf   BLOB,
  detail_plain TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  column_id    TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES board_column(id),
  sort_order   REAL NOT NULL,
  priority     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  due_at       TEXT,
  completed_at TEXT,
  created_at   TEXT NOT NULL,
  updated_at   TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE link (
  id           TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  src_type     TEXT NOT NULL,           -- note | task
  src_id       TEXT NOT NULL,
  dst_type     TEXT NOT NULL,
  dst_id       TEXT NOT NULL,
  kind         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'references',
  created_at   TEXT NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE (src_type, src_id, dst_type, dst_id, kind)
);
CREATE INDEX idx_link_src ON link(src_type, src_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_link_dst ON link(dst_type, dst_id);   -- backlinks

CREATE TABLE tag (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE note_tag (note_id TEXT, tag_id TEXT, PRIMARY KEY (note_id, tag_id));
CREATE TABLE task_tag (task_id TEXT, tag_id TEXT, PRIMARY KEY (task_id, tag_id));

CREATE TABLE open_tab (
  id           TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  kind         TEXT NOT NULL,           -- note | task
  ref_id       TEXT NOT NULL,
  sort_order   REAL NOT NULL,
  is_active    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
);

CREATE TABLE app_state (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT NOT NULL);

CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE note_fts USING fts5(title, body_plain, content='note', content_rowid='rowid');
CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE task_fts USING fts5(title, detail_plain, content='task', content_rowid='rowid');
```

### Why one generic `link` table

A typed edge table covers note→task, task→note, note→note, and task→task with one
schema, and backlinks are the reverse query on `idx_link_dst`. The alternative —
per-pair join tables — multiplies with every new linkable entity type and makes
"everything that references this" a union across N tables.

### Why `sort_order REAL`

Fractional ordering. Moving a card between two others assigns the midpoint of their
orders, so a reorder is a single-row update rather than a renumbering of the column.
A background compaction pass renormalizes when gaps get too small.

### Why RTF plus a plain shadow column

`body_rtf` gives WYSIWYG fidelity and round-trips natively through `NSAttributedString`.
`body_plain` is derived on every save and is what FTS5 indexes, so search stays fast and
never has to parse a blob. RTF also means the user's content is readable by other
applications, which an archived `AttributedString` would not be.

---

## 6. Feature design

### 6.1 Application tab rail (left)

A ~56 pt vertical rail: Notes, Tasks, Settings. Icon plus label below at the default
panel width; icon-only below 340 pt. The selected tab persists in `app_state` and is
what the panel shows on its next expand.

### 6.2 Notes

A horizontal tab strip across the top of the content area, Notepad++ style: click to
switch, drag to reorder, middle-click or `⌘W` to close, `⌘T` for a new note. The strip
scrolls horizontally with an overflow chevron listing hidden tabs, because at ~420 pt
wide only three or four tabs fit.

The editor renders `AttributedString` with a bold/italic/list/checkbox toolbar. The
primary implementation is SwiftUI's `TextEditor` with an `AttributedString` binding;
because its attribute-control surface is narrower than AppKit's, an
`NSViewRepresentable` wrapper over `NSTextView` is the fallback. Both sit behind a
single `NoteEditorView` interface so the choice is invisible to the rest of the app and
can be settled by a spike in M1 without redesign.

Open tabs are rows in `open_tab`, so the session survives a restart. `⌘P` opens quick
search over `note_fts` and `task_fts`.

### 6.3 Tasks

The Jira board mental model in a narrow panel requires a layout that adapts to width:

```
  panel < 700 pt                       panel ≥ 700 pt
  ┌────────────────────────┐           ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ ▼ Queue           (4)  │           │  Queue      Working       Done       │
  │   ┌──────────────────┐ │           │ ┌────────┐ ┌────────┐  ┌────────┐    │
  │   │ Fix edge flicker │ │           │ │ Fix    │ │ Panel  │  │ Schema │    │
  │   ├──────────────────┤ │           │ │ edge   │ │ anim   │  │ draft  │    │
  │   │ Schema review    │ │           │ ├────────┤ ├────────┤  ├────────┤    │
  │   └──────────────────┘ │           │ │ Schema │ │ Tab    │  │ Spike  │    │
  │ ▼ Working         (2)  │           │ │ review │ │ strip  │  │ RTF    │    │
  │   ┌──────────────────┐ │           │ └────────┘ └────────┘  └────────┘    │
  │   │ Panel animation  │ │           │                                      │
  │   └──────────────────┘ │           │                                      │
  │ ▶ Done            (7)  │           │                                      │
  └────────────────────────┘           └──────────────────────────────────────┘
   collapsible status groups            true side-by-side kanban
   drag between groups                  drag between columns
```

Both layouts share one drag coordinator, one drop-target model, and one reorder
operation — only the arrangement differs. Dropping a card writes `column_id` and a
fractional `sort_order`; moving into a `done`-kind column stamps `completed_at`.

Drag must suppress panel collapse for its whole duration (§4.4). A drag that ends
outside the panel is cancelled, not dropped.

### 6.4 Linking

- Typing `@` in a note or task detail opens an autocomplete popover over notes and
  tasks, ranked by recency then FTS relevance. Selecting one inserts a **link chip** —
  an attributed run carrying a custom attribute holding the target's type and id — and
  writes a `link` row.
- Dragging a task card onto an open note inserts a chip at the drop point.
- Every note and task shows a **Backlinks** section listing inbound references, which is
  a single query on `idx_link_dst`.
- Clicking a chip opens the target: notes open as a new tab, tasks open a detail sheet.
- Deleting an entity soft-deletes it and leaves its chips rendered as tombstones rather
  than silently removing text the user wrote.

### 6.5 Settings

Shell only in v1: a tab that renders a placeholder and reserves the sections the design
already implies — Activation (edge, dwell timings, hotkey), Appearance (width, theme,
material), Data (database location, export), and General (launch at login).

---

## 7. Milestones

**M0 — Shell.** `NSPanel`, hot edge monitor, state machine with suppression, tab rail,
three empty tabs, `MenuBarExtra`, global hotkey. Deliberately first: if the panel does
not feel right, nothing downstream matters.

**M1 — Notes.** NotebarKit skeleton, schema and migrations, repositories, editor spike
and decision, tab strip, persistence of open tabs, FTS search, `⌘P` quick open.

**M2 — Tasks.** Board and column seeding, task CRUD, both layouts, drag coordinator,
fractional reordering, completion stamping.

**M3 — Linking.** `@` autocomplete, link chips, `link` writes, backlinks sections,
drag-to-link, tombstones.

**M4 — Settings and polish.** Real settings, launch at login, appearance, export,
onboarding, app icon, notarized build.

---

## 8. Testing

`NotebarKit` is pure Swift with no UI imports, so it is unit-testable without a host
app — repositories against an in-memory SQLite database, link graph and backlink
resolution, fractional reorder including compaction, FTS shadow-column sync.

The panel state machine is written as a pure function over
`(state, event, context) -> (state, effects)` so the flicker cases that are painful to
reproduce by hand become ordinary table-driven tests: cursor exits and returns within
`exitDwell`; exit while typing; exit while dragging; exit while a menu is open; pin
overriding all of them; screen change mid-expansion.

UI tests cover only the flows that unit tests cannot: expand on edge, collapse on exit,
drag a card between columns, insert a link chip.

---

## 9. Open item for the author

`PanelStateMachine.shouldCollapse(...)` encodes how aggressively the panel gets out of
the way, and it is a personal-workflow judgment rather than a technical one. The
signature and the available signals are specified in §4.4; the policy is left to the
user to write, since the right answer depends on how they actually work.
